hints: Focus on what warm alkaline aqueous iodine is really testing for, the yellow precipitate of triiodomethane tells you a very specific group must be present.
For an alcohol to give a positive result it must contain the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so look for a secondary alcohol with a methyl group right next to the C-OH carbon.
Draw out the secondary $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ alcohols and check which two have that methyl-carbinol pattern, primary and tertiary alcohols can be ruled out straight away.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Great start, warm alkaline aqueous iodine is the iodoform test. A yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ means positive.

Test condition:
$$\text{warm } \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{yellow } \text{CHI}_3 \text{ precipitate if positive}$$

**Know which alcohols are positive**

Alcohols are only positive if they have the methyl-carbinol group. That is an -OH carbon joined to a $\text{CH}_3$ group.

Required group:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**List the structural alcohol isomers of $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$**

Let us sort them simply. There are 4 primary alcohols, 3 secondary alcohols and 1 tertiary alcohol.

Secondary alcohols are:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \text{ (pentan-2-ol)}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (pentan-3-ol)}$$
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3 \text{ (3-methylbutan-2-ol)}$$

**Check each secondary alcohol for the key group**

Pentan-2-ol contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so positive. Pentan-3-ol has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ on both sides of the C-OH, so no $\text{CH}_3$ directly attached, so negative.

3-methylbutan-2-ol contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so positive. Primary alcohols like pentan-1-ol and the tertiary alcohol 2-methylbutan-2-ol cannot have this group.

Count:
$$1 \text{ (pentan-2-ol)} + 1 \text{ (3-methylbutan-2-ol)} = 2 \text{ positives}$$

options.A: 0 is too low. It assumes no $\text{C}_5$ alcohol can give iodoform. In fact any alcohol containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ is oxidised by the reagent to ethanal then to triiodomethane, and such isomers do exist here.
options.B: 1 usually comes from spotting only pentan-2-ol and stopping. Students often miss the branched secondary alcohol 3-methylbutan-2-ol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3$, which also contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit.
options.C: 2 is correct. Exactly two structural isomers contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$: pentan-2-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol. Both give the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with warm $\text{I}_2$ in $\text{NaOH}$.
options.D: 3 comes from counting all three secondary alcohols as positive. Pentan-3-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is the trap. Its C-OH carbon is joined to two $\text{CH}_2$ groups, not to $\text{CH}_3$, so it cannot form iodoform.
